message.content: Cash stays liquid for the light-blue gauntlet next roll. No build, no unmortgage, no trade.
message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $426 and am on READING_RAILROAD. I own three properties with houses and one GOOJF card. p1 has $72 and is on CONNECTICUT_AVENUE with a red monopoly and dangerous dark blues.

p3 has $77 and owns yellows with one house each. p4 has $963 and fully built light blues. The bank has five houses and twelve hotels left. Mediterranean and North Carolina are unowned. I am in the post-turn action phase.

I should not sell Tennessee to p4 because that completes their orange monopoly. I will avoid unmortgaging unless necessary and instead build on St. Charles Place. Standard rent values for the light blues and pinks are being checked.

Building one house on St. Charles Place costs $100 and leaves me with $326. The pinks would then be fully equal at two houses each. p3 already paid rent on States Avenue this turn, so I am now calculating whether p4 can land on the pinks from Atlantic Avenue.

p4 on Atlantic Avenue is too far from St. Charles Place to land there immediately. p1 on Connecticut Avenue only needs a roll of 2 to reach St. Charles Place.

Rolls of 2, 4, and 5 from Connecticut Avenue all land on my pinks. If I build St. Charles Place to two houses, roll 2 alone forces p1 to liquidate. p1's dark blues are the real danger: Boardwalk at four houses pays $1700 and Park Place at three houses pays $1100.

Building St. Charles Place to two houses would raise its rent from $50 to $150. p1 has roughly an 8 in 36 chance of landing there on the next turn. If they go bankrupt, inheriting their dark blues would be a major advantage. If p4 inherits them instead, p4 becomes unstoppable.

Only St. Charles Place, States Avenue, and Virginia Avenue charge rent from Connecticut Avenue. Building St. Charles Place to two houses would raise its rent from $50 to $150, but the probability of that roll is only 1 in 36. The downside is a $100 cash outlay that may leave me short against p4's light blues.

From Reading Railroad, rolls of 2, 4, and 5 all land on p4's fully built light blues for $350 to $450. Without building St. Charles Place, a $450 hit would leave me with only about $26 after selling one house for $50.

Building St. Charles Place would actually make the light blue danger worse. A $350 hit leaves only about $26 after selling one house, and a $450 hit forces selling three houses to cover the shortfall. The cash buffer is more important than the p1 rent upgrade. I will not build.

Unmortgaging Tennessee costs $99, but its rent without a monopoly is only $14. That is a poor return on investment.

Unmortgaging Pennsylvania Railroad costs $110 for only $25 in rent. Selling houses would weaken the pink trap unnecessarily. Trading Tennessee to p4 would complete their orange monopoly, and with $963 they could unmortgage and build again.

Properties with houses cannot be traded. p4 cannot offer light blues, and p1 cannot offer dark blues without selling first. I am now considering offering cash to p1 for one of their red or dark blue properties.

p1 has no unbuilt properties to trade except Short Line, which is mortgaged and not valuable. p3 owns the full yellow set with one house on Marvin, so those cannot be traded without selling first. The GOOJF card should be kept as a safeguard rather than offered in a trade.

Jail would be strategically safe from the light blues and dark blues. I am considering a trade that hurts p4 or protects me. I want p1 to go bankrupt to me rather than to p4.

p4 on Atlantic Avenue is unlikely to land on dark blues this turn. The board is 13 spaces from Atlantic to Boardwalk, so p4 would need a roll of 11 or 13. Only 2 out of 36 rolls yields 11, and 13 is impossible. p4 is relatively safe from Boardwalk for now.

p3 is too far from dark blues to threaten them this turn. p1 owns the dark blues but does not pay rent on them. Boardwalk is safely ahead of me on Reading Railroad, so I will not land there until I lap the board. The immediate danger is the light blues next roll.

I will end the turn. I am staying liquid for the light blue gauntlet. I will post a brief, terse message.
